caveat: NO COORDINATES. The database gives prefecture, municipality and an address line, never a lat/lon, and its schema carries a position-disclosure field with a reason-for-withholding beside it. So this is a lead list: it says which trees exist and how big they are, and every pin is a separate job. Girth is the survey figure at 確認年月日, often 2000, so add the years since. Hard rule 10 still applies per tree.

leads.verify_pass_note: Verify pass 2026-09-19: confirmed this is a real, named, protected feature, not just a register address. Mt Takanosu (鷹ノ巣山, 922m) is Higashi-Hiroshima's highest point, straddling the border with Aki-Takada City. Its east summit slope carries a 4-hectare natural beech grove designated a Forestry Agency protected forest ('鷹ノ巣山ブナ・モミ希少個体群保護林'), recorded as one of the southern range limits for beech in Hiroshima Prefecture (rinya.maff.go.jp/kinki/keikaku/shinrin_keikaku/protected_cloister/protected/attach/takanosu.html). It is a real, documented hiking destination with multiple independent trail writeups (YAMAP, yamahack.com, higashihiroshima-kanko.jp). Access: trailhead is ~10 min on foot from Kenou-no-Mori campground (県央の森キャンプ場) in Fukutomi-cho, ~35 min by car from Saijo IC; summit is ~2.5 hours' hike from the trailhead. NOT resolved: exact coordinates for either tree, the trailhead itself, or even the campground (Nominatim returned nothing usable for any of them; two search attempts each). Judgement call, left as a lead rather than published: a 2.5-hour hike to an unpinned grove is not 'one obvious place to stand' in the way a shrine tree is, and the two register entries (a beech at 53630, a fir at 53631, both sharing the '鷹ノ巣山の群生林/ブナの群生林' facility label) read as two measurements inside one named natural feature rather than two separate collectible points. If this ever ships it should be ONE ensemble entry ('the beech grove near the summit of Mt Takanosu') pinned at the trailhead with the hike stated honestly as a hike, not a walk, per the island-clustering doctrine's spirit even though this isn't an island. Needs a dedicated pass with OSM/GPX trail data to get real coordinates before it can be judged as collectible.

leads.verify_pass_note: Verify pass 2026-09-19: no second source and no usable coordinate found for the 河内町 (Kochi-cho) cluster despite repeated searches (鶴亀山 河内町, 郡戸八幡神社, the town's own cultural-properties page at city.higashihiroshima.lg.jp/.../town/kochi/, and the local residents' association site youaisunkouchi.com/localinformation, which names 杉森神社 and 竹林寺 as the town's notable religious sites but neither 鶴亀山 nor 郡戸八幡神社). Nominatim returned nothing for either facility name. The shared fallback coordinate already on this record (34.5150164, 132.8360225) is confirmed still a bare 河内町 postal-area centroid, not a real fix, per the existing geocode_note; did not improve on it and it should not be used to publish. Kochi-cho is a real place (JR Sanyo Main Line stations at Kochi and Irino) but these three trees remain unlocatable at better than town level. Leave as leads for a pass that can search the Japanese-language facility names directly against a local shrine registry (広島県神社庁 lists shrines by area but the site search did not surface either name) or find an aerial/OSM natural=tree node.

coordinate_trap: THE DETAIL PAGES DO NOT PUBLISH A PER-TREE COORDINATE, and they look as though they do. Each page's inline script sets mapLat and mapLon, and 80 of these 102 records carry the identical value 37.68,140.76, which is in Fukushima, about 600 km from Hiroshima. It is the site's default map centre. The remaining 22 set it to an empty string. Scraping that field would have put an entire city's worth of trees in the wrong prefecture. Checked 2026-08-16 across all 102 records. Position here comes from geocoding the facility name and the ministry's own address instead, and every geocoded record says which of the two it got.
enriched: 2026-08-16: all 102 detail pages fetched at 1.5s intervals. The list extract had missed four fields the pages carry: 樹齢（推定）, an estimated age band, on 25 of them; 所有者・管理者区分, the owner category, on all of them; 名称（施設名）, the facility name, on 73; and the street address on 69. The owner category is the valuable one, because it answers hard rule 10 from the register itself: 72 of 102 stand on shrine or temple ground, which is the sacred-ground pattern the search doctrine says to look for first, and 20 are private.
